referral_letter: Patient is a 54-year-old male presenting with exertional chest tightness and mild shortness of breath over the past three months. Hypertension diagnosed five years ago, currently managed with amlodipine. Resting ECG shows non-specific ST changes. Family history of coronary artery disease. Referred for stress testing and cardiology review.

Patient is a 47-year-old female with a four-week history of palpitations occurring several times daily. No chest pain or syncope. History of hyperthyroidism, now resolved. Recent TSH within normal range. 24-hour Holter monitoring arranged but results pending. Referred for specialist evaluation to rule out arrhythmia.

Patient is a 61-year-old male with type 2 diabetes and hypertension presenting with progressive breathlessness on exertion. Echocardiogram at primary care level shows mild left ventricular dysfunction. Currently on metformin, lisinopril, and furosemide. Referred for further cardiac assessment and optimisation of heart failure management.

Patient is a 38-year-old female presenting with recurrent episodes of near-syncope, particularly when standing quickly. Blood pressure readings show a drop of over 20mmHg on standing. No cardiac history. Blood tests within normal limits. Referred for tilt table testing and evaluation of possible postural hypotension or dysautonomia.

Patient is a 70-year-old male with a known history of atrial fibrillation, currently on anticoagulation therapy. Presenting with increased frequency of palpitations and reduced exercise tolerance over six weeks. Recent INR was subtherapeutic on two occasions. Referred for cardiology review to reassess rhythm control strategy and anticoagulation management.

Patient is a 55-year-old male with a strong family history of sudden cardiac death. No personal cardiac history. Presenting with occasional dizziness and one episode of unexplained collapse last month. Resting ECG unremarkable. Referred urgently for comprehensive cardiac evaluation including genetic and rhythm assessment.

Patient is a 49-year-old female with poorly controlled hypertension despite being on two antihypertensive agents. Blood pressure consistently above 160/100 on multiple readings. No evidence of end-organ damage on current investigations. Renal function normal. Referred for specialist review to investigate possible secondary causes of hypertension.

Patient is a 66-year-old male post-myocardial infarction three years ago, currently on aspirin, statin, and beta-blocker. Presenting with recent onset ankle oedema and worsening fatigue. Echocardiogram requested by primary care shows reduced ejection fraction compared to baseline. Referred for cardiology follow-up and medication review.

Patient is a 43-year-old male with no prior cardiac history presenting with sharp central chest pain lasting under two minutes, relieved by rest. Pain does not radiate. Full blood count and cardiac enzymes normal. Referred for cardiology evaluation to assess for early ischaemic disease given risk factors including smoking and dyslipidaemia.

Patient is a 58-year-old female with a known bicuspid aortic valve, previously under cardiology review but lost to follow-up for three years. Presenting with new onset exertional dyspnoea. Echocardiogram at primary care suggests moderate aortic stenosis progression. Referred urgently for specialist reassessment and consideration of intervention planning.

Patient is a 52-year-old male with dyslipidaemia and a sedentary lifestyle presenting with chest heaviness during moderate activity. No prior cardiac investigations. Resting ECG normal. Referred for exercise stress testing and lipid management review. Patient is open to lifestyle modification and has expressed interest in structured cardiac rehabilitation guidance.

Patient is a 45-year-old female with newly diagnosed hypertension and incidental finding of cardiomegaly on a chest X-ray taken for unrelated respiratory complaint. No symptoms of cardiac failure. Referred for echocardiogram and cardiology review to determine aetiology and establish a monitoring and management plan.

Patient is a 34-year-old male presenting with a six-month history of left knee pain following a sports injury. MRI confirms a partial tear of the anterior cruciate ligament with associated medial meniscus damage. Physiotherapy has provided partial relief. Referred for orthopaedic assessment regarding surgical versus continued conservative management.

Patient is a 67-year-old female with severe bilateral knee osteoarthritis. Conservative management including physiotherapy, anti-inflammatory medication, and two corticosteroid injections have failed to provide adequate relief. Functional mobility is significantly impaired. X-rays show joint space narrowing and osteophyte formation. Referred for surgical consultation.

Patient is a 29-year-old male with recurrent left shoulder dislocations, the most recent requiring emergency reduction. No prior surgical intervention. MRI suggests anterior labral tear. Patient is highly active and works in a physical profession. Referred for specialist review to discuss stabilisation surgery and return-to-work planning.

Patient is a 72-year-old female who sustained a fragility fracture of the right wrist following a minor fall. DEXA scan confirms osteoporosis. Currently not on bone-protecting medication. Fracture is healing well on clinical review. Referred for orthopaedic and rheumatology input to coordinate long-term fracture prevention and bone health management.

Patient is a 41-year-old male with a three-month history of lower back pain radiating to the right leg. MRI shows L4-L5 disc herniation with nerve root compression. Conservative management with physiotherapy and analgesia has had limited effect. Referred for orthopaedic or spinal surgery consultation to discuss possible intervention.

Patient is a 55-year-old female presenting with progressive pain and stiffness in the right hip, worse in the morning and after prolonged sitting. X-rays confirm moderate hip osteoarthritis. Patient has been managing with analgesia and physiotherapy for one year without significant improvement. Referred for surgical opinion regarding hip replacement.

Patient is a 16-year-old male athlete presenting with anterior knee pain worsening during sport. Clinical findings consistent with Osgood-Schlatter disease. Physiotherapy has been initiated. Referred for specialist review as symptoms have not improved after three months and are affecting school sports participation and overall activity levels.

Patient is a 48-year-old female with carpal tunnel syndrome confirmed by nerve conduction studies. Symptoms include bilateral hand numbness and tingling, worse at night. Splinting and corticosteroid injection have provided only temporary relief. Referred for surgical consultation regarding carpal tunnel decompression, with right hand prioritised as dominant.

Patient is a 60-year-old male with a history of gout and now presenting with acute swelling and limited range of motion in the right great toe. X-rays show erosive changes consistent with chronic tophaceous gout. Urate levels elevated despite allopurinol. Referred for orthopaedic assessment and possible joint debridement or surgical intervention.

Patient is a 37-year-old female with persistent Achilles tendinopathy unresponsive to physiotherapy over five months. Ultrasound confirms tendon thickening with partial tear. The patient is a recreational runner keen to return to activity. Referred for specialist review to discuss platelet-rich plasma therapy or surgical repair options.

Patient is a 28-year-old female with a two-year history of moderate-to-severe acne affecting the face, chest, and back. Multiple topical treatments have failed. A course of oral antibiotics provided partial improvement. Quality of life and self-esteem are significantly affected. Referred for dermatology assessment regarding suitability for isotretinoin therapy.

Patient is a 45-year-old male with a six-month history of a spreading scaly rash on the scalp, elbows, and lower back. Clinical appearance is consistent with psoriasis. Topical corticosteroids have provided minimal relief. Referred for dermatology review to confirm diagnosis and initiate appropriate systemic or biologic therapy if indicated.

Patient is a 33-year-old female presenting with a rapidly changing pigmented lesion on the upper back. The lesion has increased in size and colour irregularity over approximately four months. No prior history of skin cancer. Family history of melanoma in a first-degree relative. Referred urgently for dermatoscopy and possible excision biopsy.

Patient is a 19-year-old male with a three-year history of atopic eczema affecting the flexural areas, neck, and hands. Condition has worsened with frequent flares requiring topical steroid use. Sleep is disrupted and academic performance affected. Referred for specialist review to consider dupilumab or other advanced therapies.

Patient is a 52-year-old female with chronic urticaria persisting for over six weeks. Triggers have not been identified. Antihistamines at standard and double doses have provided limited benefit. No angioedema episodes. Referred for allergy and dermatology evaluation to investigate underlying cause and consider omalizumab therapy.

Patient is a 40-year-old male presenting with diffuse non-scarring hair loss over the past eight months. Thyroid function and iron studies within normal limits. Pattern is consistent with telogen effluvium following a significant period of physical stress. Referred for dermatology review to assess for additional contributing factors and discuss treatment options.

Patient is a 61-year-old male with a longstanding history of rosacea presenting with worsening facial redness and the development of rhinophyma. Topical treatments have been used with partial effect. The patient is psychologically distressed by the appearance of the condition. Referred for specialist assessment regarding laser or surgical management.

Patient is a 25-year-old female presenting with patchy hair loss in a circular pattern on the scalp, consistent with alopecia areata. No systemic symptoms. First episode approximately six months ago with a second patch appearing recently. Referred for dermatology review to confirm diagnosis and discuss intralesional corticosteroid or other treatment options.

Patient is a 38-year-old male with a new-onset widespread blistering rash. Lesions are tense and pruritic, appearing predominantly on the trunk and limbs. Autoimmune blistering disorder is suspected. Referred urgently for dermatology evaluation and skin biopsy to establish diagnosis and initiate appropriate immunosuppressive therapy.

Patient is a 50-year-old female with a three-month history of thickened, discoloured toenails affecting multiple digits. Clinical appearance is consistent with onychomycosis. Topical antifungal treatment has been ineffective. Nail clipping sent for mycology culture. Referred for dermatology review to consider oral antifungal therapy and review culture results.

Patient is a 44-year-old male with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes and an HbA1c of 9.8%. Lifestyle modifications and metformin initiated at primary care level with limited response over three months. BMI is 34. Patient reports fatigue and increased thirst. Referred for endocrinology review to optimise glycaemic management and assess for complications.

Patient is a 31-year-old female presenting with weight gain, fatigue, cold intolerance, and constipation over the past six months. TSH is significantly elevated at 12.4 mIU/L with low free T4. Diagnosed with hypothyroidism at primary care level. Referred for endocrinology review to initiate levothyroxine therapy and provide ongoing monitoring.

Patient is a 27-year-old female with a six-month history of weight loss, tremor, heat intolerance, and anxiety. TSH is suppressed at 0.02 mIU/L with elevated free T4 and T3. Clinical features suggest Graves disease. Referred for endocrinology assessment to confirm diagnosis and discuss radioiodine, antithyroid medication, or surgical options.

Patient is a 58-year-old female with osteoporosis and an incidental finding of elevated serum calcium on a routine blood panel. Parathyroid hormone level is also elevated. Referred for endocrinology assessment to evaluate for primary hyperparathyroidism and determine whether parathyroid imaging or surgical referral is appropriate.

Patient is a 35-year-old male presenting with significant weight gain, easy bruising, facial rounding, and stretch marks over the past year. Blood pressure is elevated. Overnight dexamethasone suppression test suggests cortisol excess. Referred urgently for endocrinology evaluation and further imaging to investigate possible Cushing syndrome.

Patient is a 22-year-old female with irregular menstrual cycles, hirsutism, and acne. Ultrasound shows polycystic ovarian morphology. Testosterone and LH are mildly elevated. BMI is within normal range. Referred for endocrinology and gynaecology review to confirm diagnosis of PCOS and discuss hormonal and metabolic management options.

Patient is a 50-year-old male with type 1 diabetes presenting with recurrent unexplained hypoglycaemic episodes, including two nocturnal episodes requiring assistance. Currently on basal-bolus insulin regimen. Carbohydrate counting education previously completed. Referred for endocrinology review to consider continuous glucose monitoring or insulin pump therapy.

Patient is a 48-year-old female with a 1.8cm thyroid nodule detected incidentally on neck ultrasound. No symptoms of thyroid dysfunction. TSH within normal limits. Fine needle aspiration cytology result is indeterminate. Referred for endocrinology review to advise on further molecular testing or surgical excision to exclude malignancy.

Patient is a 39-year-old male with known adrenal insufficiency on hydrocortisone replacement presenting with recurrent adrenal crisis episodes. Patient reports poor understanding of sick day rules despite previous education. Referred for endocrinology review to reassess replacement regimen and provide structured patient education on crisis prevention and emergency management.

Patient is a 64-year-old male with long-standing type 2 diabetes and an HbA1c persistently above 10% despite three oral agents. Recent renal function shows early decline with eGFR of 52. Referred for endocrinology review to reassess the medication regimen, consider SGLT2 inhibitor or GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy, and address cardiovascular risk.

Patient is a 53-year-old male with recently identified left bundle branch block on a routine pre-employment ECG. Patient is asymptomatic. No prior cardiac history. Blood pressure and lipids within normal range. Referred for cardiology evaluation to determine whether further investigation including echocardiogram or stress imaging is required to exclude underlying structural disease.

Patient is a 44-year-old male with a four-month history of pain and reduced movement in the right shoulder. Clinical examination consistent with adhesive capsulitis. Has completed eight weeks of physiotherapy with minimal improvement. Patient requires use of the arm for occupational duties. Referred for specialist review to consider hydrodilatation or surgical capsular release.

Patient is a 55-year-old male presenting with several rough, scaly lesions on the forearms and scalp consistent with actinic keratoses. History of significant sun exposure. One lesion has developed a firm, raised border raising concern for early squamous cell carcinoma. Referred for dermatology review and possible field therapy or excision biopsy.

Patient is a 30-year-old female presenting with episodes of severe headache, sweating, and palpitations. Blood pressure during episodes is markedly elevated. 24-hour urinary metanephrines are elevated on two separate collections. Referred urgently for endocrinology assessment to investigate possible phaeochromocytoma and arrange appropriate imaging.

Patient is a 42-year-old female with a history of systemic lupus erythematosus presenting with new pleuritic chest pain and dyspnoea. D-dimer is elevated. CT pulmonary angiogram was inconclusive due to motion artifact. Referred urgently for cardiology and respiratory input to clarify the diagnosis and guide anticoagulation decision-making.

Patient is a 68-year-old male with a known rotator cuff tear diagnosed two years ago, managed conservatively. Presenting with acute worsening of right shoulder pain and inability to abduct the arm beyond 30 degrees. Repeat MRI shows significant tear progression. Referred for urgent orthopaedic review to reassess surgical candidacy.

Patient is a 47-year-old female presenting with a two-month history of painful oral ulcers and erosive lesions on the gums and inner cheeks. No skin lesions noted. Biopsy of a gingival lesion suggests mucous membrane pemphigoid. Referred for dermatology and oral medicine review to coordinate immunosuppressive therapy and prevent disease progression.

Patient is a 36-year-old male presenting with fatigue, low libido, and reduced muscle mass over approximately one year. Morning testosterone level is 6.2 nmol/L on two separate measurements, consistent with hypogonadism. LH and FSH are low, suggesting secondary hypogonadism. Referred for endocrinology assessment to investigate the underlying cause and discuss testosterone replacement therapy.
